result:
I graded `submissions/s2.json` for quiz 0001 and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s2.json`. Riley got 3 items correct, 2 partial and 1 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | Defines an agent as the loop of choosing an action, running it and feeding the result back. |
| q2 | correct | The model outputs a request naming `check_calendar` with its arguments. |
| q3 | wrong | Riley chose "left to run longer, it will eventually fix the bug", which is M6. A stuck agent needs a stopping condition such as a step limit. |
| q4 | partial | The count of 4 is right. The reasoning says the model runs the tools itself, which is M4. The program runs them. |
| q5 | correct | The result goes back as the next input, so the model can decide its next step. |
| q6 | partial | "By the name" is only part of it. The model reads the full description: name, purpose and parameters. |

**Next step:** Riley should write a description for `check_calendar` with its name, purpose and parameters. Then Riley should explain how the model would use it to choose between that tool and `search_manuals`. That also practises the program-runs-the-tools point (M4) and ties into the mission goal of writing tool descriptions.

I also wrote `learning-records/0003-quiz-0001-s2-model-requests-program-runs.md` and updated `NOTES.md`. In `NOTES.md`, s1 is still marked as not graded, since this request covered only s2.

Do you want me to grade s1 too, so we can see how the two attempts compare?
